item.title: Lyon omission in the spotlight as Australia seamers endure tough day
item.description: Australia quick Mitchell Starc claimed his 450th test wicket on Tuesday but South Africa's lower order exposed the tourists' decision to omit spinner Nathan Lyon on day three of the second test.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia quick Mitchell Starc claimed his 450th test wicket on Tuesday but South Africa's lower order exposed the tourists' decision to omit spinner Nathan Lyon on day three of the second test. Starc became only the 10th bowler to reach the milestone when Wiaan Mulder gloved a rising delivery from the 36-year-old to Matt Renshaw as South Africa slipped to 110-6. The home side then turned the tables, seeing off the all-seam attack and the back-up part-timers and making the absence of Lyon more pronounced as they went on to score 425-9 before declaring. It did not help that Josh Hazlewood, who took a career-best 6-49 in helping Australia to an emphatic 214-run victory in last week’s first test, could only bowl after lunch. He was sick on Monday, which meant he had to serve his time in the field on Tuesday before being allowed to bowl. He made little impact in nine overs, however, while captain Pat Cummins went wicketless and Starc finished with 3-89. Scott Boland, who replaced Lyon in the team, took his first five-wicket haul outside of Australia, but the tourists had to use Beau Webster to hold up an end and also turned to three other part-time spinners as South Africa piled on the runs. Lyon would have arguably done a better job of stemming South Africa's free scoring on a day when captain Temba Bavuma notched a career-best 179 to give the hosts the upper hand. "If you know you're going to be a man down from the start, you’re probably going with a different make-up, aren’t you?” Starc said. "But unfortunately Josh had a dodgy prawn or something. He'll have fresh legs for the second innings." Lyon was left to play a supporting role from the sidelines. "He's been around long enough to put his shoes back on and be the team man that he is. He was that man for most of the day today, whether it's down at fine leg running us drinks or tapping us on the back. "I’ve been left out plenty of times and naturally you're disappointed that you don't get to play. He'll get another opportunity," added Starc.

item.title: United Airlines profit outlook well below estimates, hit by fuel costs
item.description: United Airlines on Tuesday forecast fourth-quarter profit well below Wall Street estimates despite expectations for record revenue, as soaring fuel costs were expected to persist, eating into gains from strong travel demand and higher ticket prices.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Singh
item.content:encoded: United Airlines (UAL.O) on Tuesday forecast fourth-quarter profit well below Wall Street estimates despite expectations for record revenue, as soaring fuel costs were expected to persist, eating into gains from strong travel demand and higher ticket prices. Airline fares are rising sharply, but fuel costs are climbing even faster, squeezing profits industry wide. With the Iran war threatening to keep fuel prices elevated into 2027, analysts say carriers may have to raise fares further and risk losing customers, or limit flight growth to support ticket prices and protect profits. Earlier this month, United's [USN:L4N45U1TW TEXT:"rival Delta Air Lines"] (DAL.N) cut its annual earnings forecast by nearly a quarter after projecting a $6 billion increase in its fuel bill from last year. Delta CEO Ed Bastian warned that airlines may need to further restrain flight growth next year to sustain higher fares and protect profitability. United expects to pay $4.80 a gallon for jet fuel in the fourth quarter, about 45 cents more than the market consensus assumption. The difference translates into roughly $1 per share in earnings, the company said. The Chicago-based carrier expects adjusted earnings of 50 cents to $1.50 per share for the December quarter. LSEG data shows an average analyst estimate of $1.76. The $1 midpoint of the carrier's outlook is 43% below expectations. Alaska Air Group (ALK.N) added to the industry's warnings on Tuesday, forecasting a fourth-quarter adjusted loss of $2 to $2.50 per share, compared with analyst expectations for a $1.04 loss. The carrier expects its fuel bill for the year to run $1.8 billion above its original plan. Alaska's third-quarter revenue rose 14%, yet its adjusted pretax margin narrowed to 1.1% from 4.6% a year earlier. It expects revenue per unit of capacity to grow by a low-double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter, despite projecting a substantial loss. HIGHER FARES, THINNER MARGINS United's third-quarter results show how soaring fuel costs are eating into gains from higher fares. Its additional fuel spending was equivalent to nearly 70% of the increase in quarterly revenue. Despite record sales, adjusted pretax profit fell and its margin narrowed to 6.2% from 8% a year earlier. Demand, however, remains strong. United carried a record number of passengers, with revenue from business travelers, premium cabins and basic economy all growing at double-digit rates. The airline generated significantly more revenue without substantially increasing flying capacity. The squeeze extends across the industry. US air fares rose an average of nearly 23% year-on-year in the seven months through September, according to Labor Department data. The industry's fuel bill, however, has been climbing even faster. US airlines spent $42.9 billion on fuel in the first eight months of 2026, up $13.2 billion from a year earlier despite slightly lower consumption, government data showed. Analysts at Deutsche Bank have warned that further fare increases could weaken demand, forcing airlines to slow flight growth to support ticket prices. The pressure is spreading beyond the United States. Ryanair (RYA.I) CEO Michael O'Leary [USN:L6N4660EL TEXT:"warned"] on Tuesday that European airfares could rise as much as 20% next year as higher fuel costs and reduced airline capacity squeeze the industry. United and Alaska Air will discuss their financial results in separate calls with analysts and investors on Wednesday morning.

item.title: Musk calls Tesla-SpaceX merger a 'good idea' as SpaceX posts first profit as a public company
item.description: He has in the past tantalized shareholders with the idea citing growing overlap between the companies.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram, Joey Roulette
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk said on Tuesday that a merger of his two companies SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea" and that they had formed special committees to discuss a union, sending shares of the space and technology company up 4.9% in extended trading. The company earlier posted its first profit as a public company and Musk said it was tracking an annual revenue run rate of up to $1 trillion. Musk has in the past tantalized shareholders with the idea, [USN:L6N43O1D8 TEXT:"citing growing overlap"] between the companies. Speculation about SpaceX buying the EV maker has [USN:L6N46612X TEXT:"gained traction"] recently, with Barclays suggesting last week that a deal could be announced before Tesla's annual meeting in December. "I think it would be a good idea, but it's really up to the special committees of both companies," Musk said in the first official confirmation that the companies were formally talking. "Because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussion of the special committees," he told investors on a conference call. Shareholders ultimately would need to approve a deal, he added. SpaceX's revenue climbed 161% to $14.58 billion for the three months ended September 30 from a year earlier. AI revenue surged by almost 10 times to $7.56 billion, mostly from renting out data-center capacity to developers such as Anthropic, Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Reflection AI rather than from its own models. "We are in an inflection moment for SpaceX across launch, connectivity and superintelligence," Musk said on the call. He ended his portion of prepared remarks with a seemingly off-script remark: "In a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of '27 is somewhere between $500 billion and a trillion." The third quarter offered the clearest evidence yet that SpaceX’s heavy investment in AI is translating into revenue, even as spending on compute infrastructure remains enormous — capital expenses nearly tripled. The shift is reshaping a company whose financial engine has long been its Starlink internet services business and whose longer-term ambitions still hinge on getting Starship rockets into regular service. For now, though, its main business looks closer to a cloud provider's than an AI lab's. AI REVENUE DRIVES SPACEX TRANSFORMATION SpaceX's chief financial officer, Bret Johnsen, reiterated that SpaceX expects annual recurring revenue of about $100 billion by the end of 2026. He said the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditures in the fourth quarter. AI took $16.4 billion of the company's $19.6 billion in capital spending in the third quarter. "SpaceX delivered the quarter the bulls wanted, at least on the top line," said Will Rhind, CEO of asset manager GraniteShares. "The story now is all about AI. The compute contracts signed earlier this year are turning into revenue faster than a lot of people thought." The company's AI business spans Grok, social media platform X and a fast-growing data-center operation. Operating losses at the AI unit have been large and SpaceX has cautioned it will need sustained investment before it can consistently generate profits. But it turned a profit in the third quarter, compared with a year-ago loss. "With AI revenue now the company's biggest business line, the company's hyperscale business is quickly providing operating strength and leverage which will carry into the advancements of its satellite and launch business," said Daniel Newman, CEO of tech research group the Futurum Group. "Increasingly, the strength and diversification of SpaceX makes a merger with Tesla feel imminent." SpaceX reported net income of $4.4 billion versus a net loss of $1.1 billion a year earlier and analysts' expectation for a profit of $1.57 billion. On a per-share, adjusted basis, it earned 45 cents according to IBES calculations, outstripping a 13-cent average estimate. STARLINK SUBSCRIBERS TOP FORECASTS The satellite-internet unit has continued to expand its subscriber base, aided by additional satellite launches and a growing range of consumer, enterprise, aviation, maritime and government services. Starlink reached 13.6 million subscribers in the third quarter, above the 12.19 million analysts expected, but growth is coming at a price: average monthly revenue per subscriber has fallen from $99 in 2023 to $69 in the third quarter as it expands abroad with cheaper plans. The company has said geographic expansion beyond the wealthiest countries could push average revenue per user lower over time. Starship, SpaceX's next-generation reusable rocket system, has yet to enter commercial service. It is expected to enable deployment of higher-bandwidth Starlink satellites and orbital AI-computing infrastructure. The company's ability to turn Starship into a reliably reusable vehicle is central to its longer-term strategy. SpaceX successfully deployed several Starlink satellites last month, in Starship's first orbital test flight that ended hours earlier than expected after an engine issue. The space segment includes commercial launches, government missions and Starship development and remains a significant source of costs and uncertainty. Falcon launch activity has stayed robust, but revenue can vary with the mix of internal Starlink deployments, commercial customer missions and government contracts. SpaceX has increasingly prioritized launches for its own satellite network over third-party payloads, while absorbing significant costs tied to Starship's development.

item.title: FIA boss happy for F1 to race in Middle East, less sure about Dakar Rally
item.description: Formula One's governing body is happy for the last two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi to proceed as planned, despite the Iran war and conflict in the Gulf region, International Automobile Federation (FIA) president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Formula One's governing body is happy for the last two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi to proceed as planned, despite the Iran war and conflict in the Gulf region, International Automobile Federation (FIA) president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said on Tuesday. Speaking to reporters after opening a new FIA Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill, within Formula One's television headquarters, the Emirati acknowledged concern about January's Dakar Rally in Saudi Arabia but expressed confidence in F1. F1 chief executive Stefano Domenicali, who also attended the opening but did not speak to reporters, has stated the calendar is confirmed. Qatar's Lusail circuit and Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina are due to host grands prix on November 29 and December 6 respectively. Italy's Imola circuit has been mentioned as a backstop for the latter race should both Gulf rounds have to be cancelled. Asked if he felt the situation in the two countries was 'fine' at the moment, Ben Sulayem replied: 'Yeah, fine. "Does this say (mean) that there is nothing going to happen? I cannot predict this. I can only tell you today that there is nothing and the two races are going to happen." Ben Sulayem said his children remained in the Emirates and he would be happy for FIA staff to attend, adding that there were also backup plans in case some were unable to travel. SOME EVENTS IN SAUDI ARABIA HAVE BEEN CANCELLED The FIA World Rally Championship was due to end in Saudi Arabia on November 11-14 but [USN:L6N4590UY TEXT:"was cancelled"] due to the situation in the country, with the Italian round in Sardinia [USN:L6N45Q04I TEXT:"concluding the championship"] this month. The Jeddah-based rally remained automatically as part of the Middle East championship but Ben Sulayem said local organisers had asked two days ago for that to be cancelled as well. The Dakar Rally is held entirely in Saudi Arabia in January but that too has looked in doubt amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement, which has stepped up attacks on Saudi cities, airports and energy infrastructure. Some other upcoming sporting events in the kingdom have been [USN:L1N46204P TEXT:"cancelled or postponed,"] including golf, cycling and tennis. Two drivers and a team member [USN:L6N45R0VE TEXT:"told Reuters this month"] that organisers were working on an alternative route in the north of the kingdom. The current itinerary starts and finishes in King Abdullah Economic City on the Red Sea coast to the north of Jeddah and south of the key oil hub of Yanbu [USN:L1N4620VJ TEXT:"that has been targeted"]. There has also been media speculation the Dakar could be moved to Morocco. France-based Amaury Sport Organisation, organisers of the January 1-15 rally which is also the opening round of the FIA-FIM World Rally-Raid world championship, has not commented. "Up to now we are there (in Saudi)," said Ben Sulayem. "If you tell (ask) me 'is it going to happen?', I don't know. If you tell me 'is it going to be cancelled?', I don't know. There are options. Move it to Morocco, if it goes (ahead) or it doesn't go on. Common sense here (is) that we will never take our staff or drivers or any officials to a place where we feel it is risky. No way."

item.title: US FDA approves GSK's hepatitis B drug, offering patients chance to stop long-term treatment
item.description: The US FDA said on Tuesday it had approved British drugmaker GSK's hepatitis B drug Hibsago, allowing patients with the liver infection a way to keep the virus under control after stopping treatment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US FDA said on Tuesday it had approved British drugmaker GSK's (GSK.L) hepatitis B drug Hibsago, allowing patients with the liver infection a way to keep the virus under control after stopping treatment. The drug, chemically known as bepirovirsen, is the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide for chronic hepatitis B, according to the agency. Under new CEO Luke Miels, GSK is aiming to speed up the develop and launch of new medicines ahead of looming patent expirations on its blockbuster HIV drugs. The company expects [USN:L4N4241LO TEXT:"peak annual sales"] of more than £2 billion ($2.68 billion) for the drug and is central to its plans to reach more than £40 billion in annual revenue by 2031. Hibsago has already secured approval in Japan and is under regulatory review in China and Europe. The drug was licensed from rare disease drugmaker Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS.O) , which is eligible to receive milestone payments upon approval and other regulatory benchmarks. In clinical trials, bepirovirsen helped nearly one-in-five patients achieve undetectable levels of the hepatitis B virus and remain off antiviral treatment for at least six months. Hepatitis B is a serious liver infection that can lead to liver damage and cirrhosis, or scarring of the liver. The virus spreads through infected bodily fluids such as blood, saliva and semen. More than 250 million people globally live with chronic hepatitis B, and current standard-of-care treatments help only 1% to 4% of patients clear the virus for a sustained period, or achieve what doctors call a functional cure. Nucleotide analogues, a widely used class of hepatitis B treatments, are often taken for life and suppress the virus but rarely eliminate it. US biotech Aligos Therapeutics (ALGS.O) is developing a rival hepatitis B therapy, pevifoscorvir sodium, which is being evaluated in a mid-stage trial. GSK did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on US pricing and commercial availability. ($1 = 0.7474 pounds)

item.title: Anec eleva previsão de exportação de milho do Brasil em outubro; reduz a de soja
item.description: A exportação de milho do Brasil em outubro foi estimada nesta terça-feira em 6,87 milhões de toneladas, cerca de 400 mil toneladas a mais no comparativo com a previsão divulgada na semana passada, de acordo com números da Associação Nacional dos Exportadores de Cereais (Anec).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A exportação de milho do Brasil em outubro foi estimada nesta terça-feira em 6,87 milhões de toneladas, cerca de 400 mil toneladas a mais no comparativo com a previsão divulgada na semana passada, de acordo com números da Associação Nacional dos Exportadores de Cereais (Anec). O volume representa um crescimento de 1,2 milhão de toneladas em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, apontou a Anec. Já a projeção da exportação de soja foi reduzida para 6,40 milhões de toneladas em outubro, versus 6,55 milhões anteriormente. No comparativo anual, haveria uma estabilidade. Os embarques de farelo de soja do Brasil foram previstos em 2,52 milhões de toneladas até o final do mês, praticamente estáveis ante a semana anterior, representando um crescimento de quase 800 mil toneladas no comparativo anual.

item.title: Frete rodoviário sobe em setembro por pressão do diesel, aponta Edenred Mobilidade
item.description: O custo do transporte rodoviário de cargas no Brasil subiu em setembro, pressionado pela alta do diesel e pela atualização da tabela dos pisos mínimos de frete pela Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT), segundo dados divulgados nesta terça-feira pela Edenred Mobilidade.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O custo do transporte rodoviário de cargas no Brasil subiu em setembro, pressionado pela alta do diesel e pela atualização da tabela dos pisos mínimos de frete pela Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT), segundo dados divulgados nesta terça-feira pela Edenred Mobilidade. O preço médio do frete por quilômetro rodado avançou 0,57% na comparação com agosto, para R$8,77, de acordo com o Índice de Frete Rodoviário (IFR), calculado com base nas transações de frete e vale-pedágio administradas pela companhia. A alta ocorreu em um contexto de combustíveis mais caros e maior demanda por transporte ligada ao agronegócio. Segundo a Edenred, o diesel S-10 subiu 2,7% em setembro, para uma média nacional de R$7,24 por litro, enquanto o diesel comum avançou 1,33%, para R$6,84. No fim do mês, a ANTT atualizou os valores de referência usados no cálculo dos pisos mínimos de frete após a alta acumulada do diesel superar o limite previsto em lei para revisão extraordinária da tabela. "Com a fiscalização mais rigorosa do cumprimento dos pisos e da emissão do CIOT, o mercado de fretes incorporou esses ajustes", afirmou o diretor de Unidades de Negócios da Edenred Mobilidade, Vinicios Fernandes, em nota. Para outubro, a empresa vê possibilidade de pressão adicional sobre os fretes, refletindo os efeitos da atualização da tabela e o avanço do escoamento da safra agrícola.

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em alta com apoio de estrangeiros a poucos dias de eleição
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta terça-feira, rondando os 209 mil pontos no melhor momento, com bancos e B3 entre os principais suportes.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta terça-feira, rondando os 209 mil pontos no melhor momento, com bancos e B3 entre os principais suportes. A bolsa paulista continua em clima de expectativa para o desfecho da eleição presidencial no país, com o segundo turno no domingo, enquanto investidores estrangeiros continuam fornecendo apoio para as ações brasileiras. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) avançou 1,57%, a 208.295,98 pontos, chegando a 208.941,57 na máxima e marcando 205.082,26 na mínima do dia. O volume financeiro no pregão somou R$42,5 bilhões. "Trade eleitoral", resumiu o sócio e advisor da Blue3 Investimentos, Willian Queiroz, sobre o desempenho do Ibovespa. Ele destacou que, embora as pesquisas ainda mostrem um cenário acirrado na disputa entre o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) pelo Palácio do Planalto, o candidato do PL continua à frente. Ações na B3 têm reagido positivamente a uma potencial troca em Brasília em razão de expectativas principalmente de melhora no cenário fiscal do país. Apenas em outubro, impulsionado principalmente pelo resultado do primeiro turno da eleição, com Flávio à frente, a B3 registra um saldo de capital externo positivo de R$20,99 bilhões até o dia 16. O exterior corroborou o avanço do Ibovespa, com o norte-americano S&P 500 (.SPX) fechando em alta de 0,28%, enquanto o rendimento dos títulos de 10 anos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos marcava 5,1126% no final do dia, de 5,136% na véspera. DESTAQUES BTG PACTUAL UNIT subiu 4,36%, melhor desempenho entre os bancos do Ibovespa, que têm se mostrado sensíveis às expectativas eleitorais. BRADESCO PN , que reporta balanço no final da quinta-feira, avançou 2,89%, ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN valorizou-se 1,88%, BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) fechou com elevação de 1,04% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT apurou acréscimo de 1,26%. No radar do setor, fontes afirmaram à Reuters que o Banco Central prepara [USN:L1N4650WU TEXT:"medidas"] para conter o crescente endividamento das famílias, incluindo ações para ampliar responsabilidades e exigir transparência por parte dos bancos, e analisa um modelo regulatório que limita o crédito autorizado por pessoa a depender do nível de renda. B3 ON (B3SA3.SA) valorizou-se 5,38%, também refletindo o potencial efeito no mercado em razão das expectativas envolvendo o desfecho eleitoral. Dados recentes já têm mostrado melhora no volume negociado em renda variável, além de fluxo positivo de estrangeiros. PETROBRAS PN avançou 0,36% e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) subiu 0,48%. O Brasil ultrapassou a Arábia Saudita como o segundo maior [USN:L6N4660QF TEXT:"fornecedor"] de petróleo bruto para a China nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, segundo dados alfandegários divulgados pelo país asiático nesta terça-feira. No exterior, o barril de petróleo sob o contrato Brent fechou a US$108,79, queda de 0,69%. VALE ON (VALE3.SA) recuou 1,39%, em linha com a fraqueza dos futuros do [USN:L6N4660RV TEXT:"minério de ferro"] na China. A mineradora informou nesta terça-feira que apresentou um pedido à Associação Nacional de Investidores Institucionais do Mercado Financeiro da China (NAFMII) para o registro de um programa de títulos de dívida "[USN:S0N44L00Q TEXT:"Panda Bonds"]" na China. O programa envolve títulos denominados em renminbi para o período de 2026 a 2028, com montante principal agregado de até RMB 10 bilhões. Os títulos emitidos no âmbito desse programa serão integral e incondicionalmente garantidos pela companhia. MAGAZINE LUIZA ON (MGLU3.SA) disparou 14,79%, com o setor sensível a juros entre os destaques positivos em pregão com [USN:L1N4660X3 TEXT:"alívio"] na curva de juros brasileira. O amplo índice de consumo (.ICON) da B3 subiu 3,3%. ÂNIMA EDUCAÇÃO ON (ANIM3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, caiu 9,19%, após [USN:L1N465104 TEXT:"acordo"] da sua subsidiária de ensino de medicina Inspirali com o grupo de educação médica do Einstein para usar a marca do hospital em seus cursos a partir do próximo ano. O acordo de 20 anos envolve um pagamento fixo ao Einstein de R$150 milhões e pagamentos de 6% da receita líquida de novos alunos de medicina, entre outros detalhes. JSL ON (JSLG3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, subiu 6,83%, tendo ainda no radar prévia de resultados mostrando [USN:S0N45000S TEXT:"receita bruta"] de R$3,09 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 5,9% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. AMERICANAS ON (AMER3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, disparou 15,58%, após a Justiça do Rio de Janeiro decretar o [USN:L1N465112 TEXT:"encerramento"] do processo de recuperação judicial da companhia.

item.title: Netflix co-CEO Sarandos says 'we could do better' after weak forecast
item.description: Netflix issued weaker-than-expected guidance for fourth-quarter profit and cut its full-year advertising forecast on Tuesday, days after the streaming pioneer laid off 6% of its workforce and replaced two of its top programming executives.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Richwine, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Netflix (NFLX.O) issued weaker-than-expected guidance for fourth-quarter profit and cut its full-year advertising forecast on Tuesday, days after the streaming pioneer laid off 6% of its workforce and replaced two of its top programming executives. Shares of Netflix fell nearly 6% to $64.66 in after-hours trading. The stock had fallen more than 40% in a year before the earnings report. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos said the company plans to focus on its core business of producing quality TV shows and movies to make Netflix a must-have service, and the recent executive shakeup was a step toward that goal. "I know that we could do better," Sarandos said in a post-earnings video call. "Now we've seen an opportunity to take our slate to the next level." Third-quarter revenue rose 11.8% to $12.87 billion, in line with Wall Street forecasts, but the lowest rate of increase in nearly three years. The company forecast fourth-quarter net income of $2.79 billion and EPS of 67 cents, below the average analyst forecast of $3.07 billion and 73 cents. Netflix reduced its advertising forecast for 2026 to roughly $2.7 billion, down from about $3 billion. Some ad product capabilities rolled out slightly slower than expected, executives said in their quarterly letter to shareholders. The company that shook up Hollywood when it started streaming TV shows and movies two decades ago is now competing with a surge in viewership on YouTube and TikTok. Netflix has invested in video games, podcasts and live events to draw new viewers and increase the time members spend on the platform. Wall Street analysts have questioned how the company will kick-start growth. "Netflix remains a well-oiled, highly profitable machine, but focused on too many unwanted distractions," PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore said. "The company needs to get back to basics and focus on compelling content." In its earnings report, Netflix said it would continue to expand its offerings through licensing more third-party content. For the third quarter, earnings per share came in at 87 cents, ahead of the 82-cent average forecast of analysts surveyed by LSEG. New programming during the quarter included "Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story," the second season of "The Gentlemen," the final installment of "Outer Banks" and a reboot of "Little House on the Prairie." Last week, Netflix [USN:L6N4600X7 TEXT:"laid off 1,000 people"], or about 6% of its employees. The company replaced Chief Creative Officer Bela [USN:L4N46128P TEXT:"Bajaria"] and said film chief [USN:L4N4651E5 TEXT:"Dan Lin was departing"], signs that it is resetting its programming strategy. The company named former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice to replace Bajaria. He also will oversee the film division until a replacement for Lin is chosen. "Peter Rice understands talent relations, and in a competitive market, creative talent have choices of where they want to work," Sarandos said on Tuesday. "We want Netflix to always be the place that they love to do the best work of their life." Earlier this year, Netflix lost a bidding war for Warner Bros Discovery and its rich library of characters, which was sold to David Ellison-led Skydance . Some analysts believe Netflix could go after other acquisition targets such as NBCUniversal after Comcast (CMCSA.O) spins it off. Netflix has posted monthly subscriber losses in the US throughout 2026, with no net additions reported for any month up to September, data from analytics firm Antenna showed. Antenna tracks US subscription purchases via sources like credit card transactions, but excludes subscriptions acquired through wholesale bundles. A Netflix spokesperson said the Antenna data were "not representative of Netflix's business performance." Sarandos said there was no need for a "fundamental shift" in strategy but added: "We do need better execution in the US."

item.title: トランプ氏 、加ボンバルディア排除の脅し撤回 カンザス州の雇用「守る」
item.description:
David Shepardson Allison Lampert
[ワシントン／モントリオール ２０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
David Shepardson　Allison Lampert

[ワシントン／モントリオール ２０日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２０日、カナダの航空機メーカーであるボンバルディアを米市場から締め出すとの脅しを撤回し、代わりにカンザス州の同社従業員を「しっかり守る」と約束した。

トランプ氏が９月にボンバルディアの米市場での販売禁止を示唆したことは、ウィチタで１５００人を雇用するカンザス州で政治問題化していた。販売禁止の脅しを受け、共和党のロジャー・マーシャル上院議員らカンザス州選出の議員は、ホワイトハウスに働きかけを行った。

トランプ氏はカンザス州の「１２ニュース」に対し、マーシャル氏の関与に言及しつつ、「ボンバルディアを守る」と述べた。その上で「ある航空会社の立て直しを手伝うつもりだ。私はずっと彼らをカナダ企業と見なしてきた」と説明。「しかし今、同社が米国内に拠点を置いていることが分かった。カンザス州にいるのなら彼らを傷つけるつもりはない。従業員と雇用を守るつもりだ」と述べた。

トランプ氏の発言を受け、ボンバルディアの株価は一時、４％上昇した。

ホワイトハウスはコメントを控え、質問についてはトランプ氏のテレビインタビューを参照するよう求めた。

item.title: League says Eagles handled Hurts medical condition appropriately
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles handled Jalen Hurts' medical condition appropriately, an NFL spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday, after the quarterback was sidelined indefinitely due to blood clots in his lungs.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia Eagles handled Jalen Hurts' medical condition appropriately, an NFL spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday, after the quarterback was sidelined indefinitely due to blood clots in his lungs. Hurts was diagnosed with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis prior to playing in an October 11 contest against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. After further testing and monitoring, he was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and a bilateral pulmonary embolism, [USN:L6N4650YZ TEXT:"the team said"] on Monday. The NFL had stayed in close contact with the team, the spokesperson said, and found that the Eagles had handled the matter appropriately, after a day of outcry from many pundits and fans, who questioned why Hurts was allowed to play at all in the London game. The 2025 Super Bowl MVP is clinically stable as he undergoes treatment with blood thinners, but he is expected to be out for the season. A bilateral pulmonary embolism is a dangerous condition in which a blood clot blocks an artery in both lungs. The NFL was in contact with Eagles medical personnel and the Cleveland Clinic in London, where Hurts was tested. The league's chief medical officer arranges medical resources in every international market with approval from the players' union, the spokesperson added. NFL owners gathered in New York on Tuesday for their fall meeting amid an ambitious international slate of games this season, with a record nine contests abroad. League officials were critical of early media reports and speculation surrounding Hurts' condition, telling reporters at a press conference on Tuesday that doctors caring for players are not ever influenced by coaches, general managers or team owners. "If you're not sitting in that room with that patient and you don't have all the data, if you are speculating as a physician on what should have been done, you are unprofessional and unethical in doing that," said NFL Chief Medical Officer Allen Sills. Sills said there was no set league protocol for blood clots, as there is with concussions. "I have complete confidence in the Eagles staff and their handling of this situation," he added. "I would characterize their work as very conservative, very patient, focused and appropriately guarded at every step."

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル下落、ＡＩ懸念が重し 円は20年債入札好調で上昇
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ２０日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。ドルは原...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル下落、ＡＩ懸念が重し　円は20年債入札好調で上昇 4:48 配信

３月２４日撮影　REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

［ニューヨーク　２０日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。ドルは原油価格と米長期債利回りの低下に歩調を合わせるように下落。市場では、米国とイランの対立激化による影響のほか、米国のＡＩ（人工知能）関連企業に対する旺盛な資本流入が持続可能性が注目されている。

終盤の取引で、円は対ドルで０．２１％高の１５８．１４円。日本の財務省が実施した２０年利付国債入札で応札倍率が５．８４倍と、前回（４．０１倍）から大幅に上昇し、同入札としては過去最高を付けたことが円の支援材料になった。

ステート・ストリート・インベストメント・マネジメントのシニア債券ストラテジスト、マサヒコ・ルー氏は「２０年債入札に対する記録的な需要は、待機資金がついに市場に戻り始めたことを示す強いシグナルになる」と指摘。「フランスの政治・財政面での不透明感を背景に、資金の安全な逃避先として日本国債の魅力が相対的に高まりつつある」と述べた。

主要６通貨に対するドル指数は０．２５％安１０１．７１。ユーロは対ドルで０．２２％高の１．１２３５ドル。

この日は原油価格が一時５カ月ぶりの高値を付けた後、下落。ただ、市場ではＡＩを巡る懸念がより大きく意識されている。野村証券のＧ１０通貨戦略責任者、ドミニク・バニング氏は、「エネルギー価格の上昇はドル相場にとって追い風になるが、金利がＡＩ関連取引を崩壊させるほど高い水準に達すれば、ドル相場にとってマイナスの影響を及ぼすことになる」と指摘。「現在はまさにその境目となる水準が試されているところだ」としている。

ユーロはこの日の取引では対ドルで上昇したものの、市場ではフランスの財政状況の悪化や各地で広がる抗議活動への警戒感から、ユーロに対する慎重な見方が根強い。スウェーデンのハンデルスバンケンの外国為替ストラテジスト、トミー・フォンブロムセン氏は「フランスを巡る懸念はすぐには解消されない」と指摘。「フランスに対する弱気な見方は当面続くと見られるため、ユーロには一段の下落余地がある」と述べた。

カナダドルは対米ドルで０．３４％高の１．４０６カナダドルと、約１カ月ぶりの高水準を付けた。 カナダ西部アルバータ州で１９日に実施された分離独立を問う住民投票でカナダへの残留が支持され、国内の結束を図るカーニー首相にとって待望の勝利となった。

Oct 20 : Real Madrid are seeking contributions towards the setup costs of the failed European Super League project from the six Premier League clubs that withdrew shortly after its launch, the Spanish side confirmed to Reuters on Tuesday. The Athletic reported that the total costs could reach €80 million ($89.9 million). Real are seeking payments from Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur. The six were among nine of the competition's 12 founding clubs that withdrew within three days of its launch in 2021 amid widespread opposition. Real did not immediately confirm whether they were also seeking payments from the other three early leavers, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid.

Real Madrid said the six English clubs were liable for costs incurred in establishing the competition, which have so far been covered by Juventus, Barcelona and Real. Tottenham declined to comment while the other five Premier League clubs did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The Athletic reported that the clubs signed a shareholders' agreement for the European Super League Company, the holding company behind the competition, although it is unclear whether the contract explicitly set out their liability for setup costs. The Super League collapsed shortly after its launch following the withdrawal of the nine clubs. Juventus subsequently pulled out of the project and Barcelona formally withdrew in February, leaving Real Madrid as its sole remaining founding club. Real, UEFA and European Football Clubs announced an agreement of principles on February 11 aimed at resolving their Super League-related legal disputes. ($1 = 0.8903 euros)

item.title: Anthropic logged net loss of over $80 billion in first half of 2026, WSJ reports
item.description: Anthropic reported a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of the year and signaled it could spend as much as $750 billion in the coming years to secure more computing capacity, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic reported a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of the year and signaled it could spend as much as $750 billion in the coming years to secure more computing capacity, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday. The loss, up from $13 billion a year earlier, was driven by $72 billion in accounting charges tied to changes in the value of financial instruments Anthropic issued to raise money, the report said, citing a draft prospectus for its IPO. The figures show the hefty costs of the AI race even as investors look harder at whether the money companies are pouring into chips and data centers will pay off. Anthropic's revenue jumped to $16.3 billion in the six months ended June 30 from $1.1 billion a year ago, while AI infrastructure spending nearly quadrupled to almost $9 billion, the Journal said. Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment and Reuters could not immediately verify the report. ANTHROPIC'S IPO VALUATION UNDER SCRUTINY Reuters reported first in September that Anthropic posted a net loss of [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"$42 billion in 2025"], as part of a series of exclusives from its IPO prospectus. The company has benefited from the popularity of Claude Code, its coding assistant that developers use to write software and build apps. But some current investors and prospective investors who attended Anthropic's investor day last week are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter [USN:L6N4611F6 TEXT:"had told Reuters"]. The investors who attended the event in San Francisco discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, three of the people had said, a significant step down from the roughly $2 trillion valuation previously expected for the November share sale. Anthropic told investors at the meeting that its third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis during the quarter. A cooler reception for Anthropic's IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale's success, ahead of rival OpenAI's potential listing next year.

item.title: FAA certifies Boeing's 737 MAX 10, clearing way for deliveries
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration on Tuesday granted final approval to the long-delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10, clearing the way for the US planemaker to begin delivering the largest version of its best-selling airplane.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The Federal Aviation Administration on Tuesday granted final approval to the long-delayed Boeing (BA.N) 737 MAX 10, clearing the way for the US planemaker to begin delivering the largest version of its best-selling airplane. Boeing has said the MAX 10 will be a major driver of cash flow in its ongoing financial recovery following years of crises and controversies that slowed the company's timeline for the MAX 10. So far, airlines have ordered more than 1,550 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for 31% of Boeing's outstanding 737 backlog, according to IBA, an aviation analytics consultancy. The plane is critical to Boeing's fight with Airbus (AIR.PA) for orders in the lucrative single-aisle jetliner market, with China's COMAC C919 in a distant third place. "We want to beat the Europeans, we want to beat the Chinese," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Tuesday at Boeing's plant in Everett, Washington, to tout the FAA certification. "But if we want to continue to do that, I have to allow you all to certify aircraft faster," Duffy said, a nod to his promise to streamline airplane certification. Boeing has been trying to certify the 737 MAX 10 since the early 2020s. In July, the company opened a new production line at the Everett plant to increase 737 output, which it also assembles in nearby Renton. Stephanie Pope, president and CEO of Boeing Commercial Airplanes, said deliveries will begin in the coming months, adding that the MAX 10 "offers greater capacity, longer range and the best seat economics in its class." The largest MAX 10 can hold up to 230 passengers, compared with up to 195 for the MAX 9 and 160 for the MAX 7. However, the delays have helped European rival Airbus' (AIR.PA) A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market. The bigger, higher-capacity plane is crucial to several airlines' growth plans. Major customers for the MAX 10 include United Airlines (UAL.O) , Alaska Airlines (ALK.N) , Ryanair (RYA.I) , Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) and American Airlines (AAL.O) . The planemaker has already built a handful of MAX 10s awaiting delivery. Boeing has faced a more stringent certification process since two fatal MAX 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019 killed 346 people. Scrutiny of the company's production and quality systems also increased after a January 2024 mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9. The FAA in August approved the smaller 737 MAX 7 after a review that lasted more than eight years. The regulator required the MAX 10 to include significant improvements, including updates to the flight control system with an enhanced angle-of-attack sensor. Those will be applied to the existing fleet in the coming years. A problem with the anti-ice system on 737 MAX engines that arose in 2023 further delayed certification of the MAX 7 and 10. Boeing disclosed another glitch in late September with the latest update of the 737 MAX's navigation software, which threatened to further delay certification. However, the FAA determined it did not pose a safety concern and did not require Boeing to fix the problem as a condition of certifying the plane. Boeing is still working on certifying the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production, which is six years behind schedule. The company has said it expects to complete certification and begin deliveries in 2027.

FAST

GQEBERHA, South Africa, Oct 20 : South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said he enjoyed battling against adversity as he scored 179 on Tuesday to turn around his side’s fortunes in the second test against Australia and also quell some of his own mental demons. The captain produced a defiant display and showcased his batting skills as South Africa recovered from a precarious 110-6 in the morning session on the third day to declare on 425-9 before taking an Australian wicket prior to stumps, an emphatic response to their heavy defeat in last week’s first test. The 36-year-old Bavuma had been forced to the crease with the hosts on 12-2 on Sunday’s rain-restricted opening day, when only an hour's play was possible, and had to resume his innings on Monday as the ball moved around after the wet weather finally relented. South Africa slumped to 97-5 by the close of the second day. “I walked into a tricky situation,” he told reporters. “I think everything was in the bowlers’ favour, the conditions overhead, the wicket itself, we’d just lost two early wickets, but ordinarily I’ve found myself in those situations quite a number of times and I guess it seems to bring out the best in me."

The sun appeared on Tuesday after two rain-affected days and the pitch flattened out, offering the batters considerably more assistance, although Bavuma insisted conditions were not as easy as they might have seemed. DEALING WITH AUSTRALIA’S QUALITY ATTACK “With the quality of the bowling attack, they're still able to put you under pressure, even when the ball is slightly softer and older. “I think from a mindset point of view, for me, nothing really changed. I was always just trying to be as tight as I could and try to hit the ball as straight as I could. “The one thing was being able to get the team out of a tough situation. But then from a personal point of view, to go on to getting a big 100, that's obviously something that's been a thorn in my side throughout my career. So it was nice to get over that mental hurdle,” he added. Bavuma, who has overcome a long-standing elbow injury, not only surpassed his previous highest test score but featured in two record partnerships. He added 132 with Marco Jansen, who scored 85, to set a South African seventh-wicket record at St George’s Park, before putting on a national-record 183 for the eighth wicket with number nine Simon Harmer, who made a test career-best 82. “They put a heavy price on their wickets and part of our plan was to keep Australia in the field for as long as we could. It all went according to plan,” Bavuma added as Australia will resume at 3–1 at the start of day four.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（20日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
続落して取引を終えた。銀行株や資源関連株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に続落。中型株で構成す...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（20日） 4:18 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。銀行株や資源関連株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に続落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．０６％安だった。

英労働市場統計によると、賃金上昇ペースはわずかに加速し、雇用に回復の兆しが見られた。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場ではイングランド銀行（英中央銀行）が１１月に０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決めることがほぼ確実視されている。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は０．８４％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣ、ナットウエスト、ロイズは０．９─１．１％下落した。

資源株指数は１．５９％下落。石油大手のＢＰは１．７％、シェルは０．８％それぞれ下落した。

一方、公益事業株指数は１．５２％高。電力・ガス供給のナショナル・グリッドは１．８％上昇した。住宅建設株指数は３．２９％高。

ＪＰモルガンが目標株価を引き上げたオンラインスーパー大手オカドは１０．０％上昇した。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連投資への懸念などから、工業株の売り注文が優勢だった。フランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は０．３８％安と続落。経済の停滞や財政悪化といった課題を抱えるフランスで、激しい抗議デモが発生。約半年後に大統領選を控えることもあり、投資家の警戒感が強まっている。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種工業株指数は１．４３％安。データセンター関連を顧客とするスイス重電大手ＡＢＢは５．０％安。機関投資家から資金調達を実施した配電・制御機器大手シュナイダー・エレクトリックは３．３％下落。

一方、フランスのクラウド事業者のＯＶＨクラウドは１８．０％高。財務指標が改善し、買われた。直近の四半期決算が増収だった電子機器メーカーのコメット・ホールディングは４．７％上昇した。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場では、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が今月の理事会で金利を据え置いた後、１２月会合で利上げを決めることが有力視されている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

フランス国債利回りが２４年ぶりの高水準近辺で推移した。抗議デモの拡大懸念を背景に前日は約1カ月ぶりの大幅上昇を記録し、この日も荒い値動きが続いた。終盤には小幅低下した。

フランス１０年国債（ＯＡＴ）利回りは終盤に３ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の４．８８％。一時４．９８７７％まで上昇し、２００２年７月以来の高水準となった１０月初旬の４．９９３７％に迫った。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は約２．５ｂｐ拡大し、１５０ｂｐとなった。この利回り格差は１０月初旬に１５８．６７ｂｐと、２０１１年１１月以来の水準に拡大していた。

ゴールドマン・サックスのストラテジストらは「直接的な経済への影響は当面限定的にとどまるとみているが、混乱がさらに広がる可能性は、金融環境の引き締まり、政治的不確実性の高まり、緊縮財政によって既に弱まっている経済に、新たな逆風をもたらす」と指摘した。

一方、ユーロ圏の指標となるドイツ国債の利回りは低下したものの、最近のレンジ内にとどまった。エネルギー価格の上昇圧力が根強く、投資家は欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の追加利上げ観測を後退させていない。

ドイツ１０年国債利回りは７ｂｐ低下の３．３８５％。

政策金利見通しに敏感なドイツ２年国債利回りは５ｂｐ低下し、３．０４５％となった。

独伊１０年債利回り格差は１．５７ｂｐ縮小し、１０９．５ｂｐとなった。

ユーロ圏金融・債券市場：[DE/BJ]

item.title: トランプ氏、ウクライナに和平合意促す ロシア拘束の米国人巡る進展示唆
item.description:
Steve Holland Trevor Hunnicutt
[ワシントン ２０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Steve Holland　Trevor Hunnicutt

[ワシントン　２０日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２０日、ロシアとの戦争終結に向け、ウクライナに和平合意に応じるよう求めた。

トランプ氏はホワイトハウスの大統領執務室で記者団に対し、「ウクライナはこの戦争を終わらせたいと望まなければならない」と述べた。また、「ウクライナがこの戦争を終わらせるときが来た」とし、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領が合意に応じることを望んでいると語った。

その上で、ロシアは戦場で優位に立っているとの認識を表明。「ロシアは巨大な機械のようなもので、ただ前進し続けており、実際にそうしてきた」とし、「ロシアは非常に広い領土を占領した」と述べた。

トランプ氏はまた、ロシアで拘束されている米国人の元教師、スティーブン・ハバード氏の問題について、ロシアのプーチン大統領と協議したと明らかにし、この件について近く進展がある可能性を示唆した。

トランプ氏は、ハバード氏に関する記者団の質問に対し「プーチン氏とこの件について話をしている」とし、「何が起きるか見ていてほしい。われわれはハバード氏の問題に集中して取り組んできた」と述べた。

ハバード氏は７４歳で、傭兵活動に関する罪で有罪判決を受けロシアの刑務所で約７年の刑に服している。米国務省はハバード氏の件を不当拘束と認定している。

ゼレンスキー大統領はこの日、ノルウェーの首都オスロで米国のウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使と会談。会談後の記者会見で、ロシアによる弾道ミサイル攻撃に関する情報共有や早期警戒の提供を米国が再開したことに謝意を示した。

ノルウェーのストーレ首相によると、ウィットコフ氏は２１日にロシア第２の都市サンクトペテルブルクを訪問し、ロシア首脳部と会談する。

item.title: At least 17 data center campuses proposed on US public lands, group says
item.description: At least 35 data center-related applications covering more than 24,000 acres of US federal land are pending or active across six Western states, according to an analysis by conservation group Center for Western Priorities.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 35 data center-related applications covering more than 24,000 acres of US federal land are pending or active across six Western states, according to an analysis by conservation group Center for Western Priorities. US Bureau of Land Management records show at least 17 proposed data center campuses and 13 related infrastructure projects, including transmission lines, pipelines, telecommunications facilities and access roads across Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon, Utah and Wyoming, according to the study. A map of the planned projects includes several applications for infrastructure tied to a Prometheus Hyperscale facility in Wyoming and a range of projects by developer Copia Power in Arizona, Nevada and Idaho, among others. The figures underscore industry interest in developing AI infrastructure on federal land as the Trump administration seeks to open public lands to a wider range of industrial uses, including energy, mining and technology projects. US President Donald Trump's administration has strongly [USN:L8N3ZL04J TEXT:"backed"] data center expansion as a national priority, but the public is increasingly [USN:L1N3WX0S4 TEXT:"opposed"] to such projects, citing concerns about electricity demand, water consumption, wildlife impacts and public access to federal lands. BLM officials were not immediately available for comment.

item.title: Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections
item.description: President Donald Trump’s record-low popularity, voter frustration over the cost of living and a fierce immigration fight are shaping the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine whether Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats gain the power to challenge his administration.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Mccaskill
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump’s record-low popularity, voter frustration over the cost of living and a fierce immigration fight are shaping the November 3 midterm elections , which will determine whether Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats gain the power to challenge his administration. Republicans hold narrow majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of each chamber. The outcome will hinge on a relatively small number of competitive races, but the campaigns are being shaped nationally by Trump himself and voter concerns over affordability and immigration. Here is a look at the three issues defining the election: DONALD TRUMP The president has put himself front and center in the closing stretch of the campaign cycle despite his record-low popularity, with upcoming rallies in Florida, Iowa, Michigan and Texas. Trump's approval rating has fallen to an all-time low 31%, according to a [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. Yet he has repeatedly urged voters to pretend he's on the ballot, an effort that could motivate Democrats and independents to rally against his party despite the message being aimed at increasing turnout among Trump's base. Democrats have said Trump has broken his campaign promises to lower costs and end wars. They have vowed to tackle an affordability agenda to reduce Americans' cost of living and hold the administration accountable for alleged corruption if voters give them control of either chamber. AFFORDABILITY Voters have consistently ranked the cost of living as the top issue this election cycle. Half of registered voters surveyed in a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll cited the cost of living as the most important factor in how they will vote. In the same poll, voters highlighted healthcare, gasoline, food and housing as the top household bills lawmakers should focus on. Republicans' top legislative achievement was a tax cut extension that slashed roughly $1 trillion in spending for Medicaid, the government health insurance program for low-income Americans, and other health programs. Democrats last year forced a government shutdown over a failed effort to extend expiring health subsidies that benefited 24 million Americans. Gas prices have spiked since the US and Israel launched military strikes on Iran in February. The national average price of gas is $4.28 — $1.20 higher than it was a year ago, according to AAA. The average cost of diesel is $6.32 — a $2.70 increase from a year earlier. Grocery costs are up 1.8% over the past year, according to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics data on consumer prices. Federal Housing Finance Agency data show home prices rose 2.1% over the past year. Congress passed a bipartisan housing bill earlier this year. It became law without Trump's signature. IMMIGRATION Preliminary data from the Department of Homeland Security showed a 95% drop in migrants apprehended at the southwest border compared to former President Joe Biden's administration. The agency said there have been no Border Patrol releases the entire fiscal year for the first time ever. But fatal encounters with federal immigration agents have occurred in Maine, Minnesota and Texas. The backlash to the death of two US citizens in Minnesota pulled many Democrats in competitive primaries to the left this year, with some candidates calling for the impeachment of then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and others saying Immigration and Customs Enforcement should be abolished. Democrats and Republicans sparred over immigration funding this year in a stalemate that forced Republicans to unilaterally pass a $70 billion bill to fund ICE and the Border Patrol for the remainder of Trump's presidency. Republicans counter Democrats' criticism by saying Democrats support open borders. Federal immigration officials also [USN:L1N45Y0CB TEXT:"raided the Washington home"] of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota this month, drawing widespread condemnation from Democrats. A person familiar with the case against Omar told Reuters one potential aim of the investigation could be to [USN:L6N46118Z TEXT:"strip her of US citizenship and deport her"]. OTHER ISSUES Artificial intelligence and data centers, cryptocurrency, abortion and Israel could also influence voters in individual races. In Ohio's Senate race, for example, Democratic nominee Sherrod Brown has labeled Republican Senator Jon Husted the face of data centers, and the crypto super PAC Defend American Jobs has spent more than $46 million to reelect Husted over Brown, a former US senator who chaired the chamber's Banking Committee. In Maine's Senate race, Democratic nominee Troy Jackson is hoping voters don't forget that Republican Senator Susan Collins helped confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court, which later overturned the federal right to abortion. Collins is on the election ballot for the first time since the high court made abortion a state issue rather than a federal right. In Michigan, Republican nominee Mike Rogers has indicated he would accept help from a pro-Israel super PAC that spent more than $30 million backing Democratic US Representative Haley Stevens in her unsuccessful primary against Abdul El-Sayed, who now faces Rogers in the general election. The group has already spent more than $280,000 on mailers against El-Sayed. Earlier this week, Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection.

item.title: EQT in advanced talks to buy testing firm Qiagen, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: European molecular testing company Qiagen is in advanced talks to be acquired by Swedish buyout firm EQT , Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Sahil Pandey
item.content:encoded: European molecular testing company Qiagen (QIA.DE) is in advanced talks to be acquired by Swedish buyout firm EQT (EQTAB.ST) , Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. US-listed shares of Qiagen were up over 6% in afternoon trading. The company has a market capitalization of €8.57 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Qiagen's board is meeting this week to decide on the potential deal, the report said, citing people familiar with the talks. There is no certainty the discussions will lead to a sale to EQT or another buyer, the report added. EQT has submitted a binding offer of more than $50 per share for Qiagen, while US private equity firm KKR has also made a bid, Bloomberg News reported. The reported talks come after Qiagen said [USN:L4N3YL1R1 TEXT:"in January"] it was evaluating strategic options amid renewed takeover interest. Interest in the diagnostics company continued through the year, with buyout firms including EQT, Advent and KKR linked to a potential acquisition in July. Barclays analyst Luke Sergott said the latest Bloomberg report suggests a deal appears "more likely" and that he continues to see "a good possibility that a deal goes through." Sergott reiterated his $55 price target on Qiagen. Qiagen develops molecular testing and sample-preparation technologies used by research and clinical laboratories. KKR declined to comment, while EQT did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. Qiagen said it does not comment on "market rumors or speculation." ($1 = 0.9259 euros)

item.title: iFood compra empresa de benefícios Caju e dobra presença no setor de vales-alimentação
item.description: O iFood, aplicativo de entrega de comida controlado pela investidora holandesa Prosus , anunciou nesta terça-feira a compra da Caju, empresa de benefícios corporativos e atuante no mercado de vales-refeição e vales-alimentação.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: O iFood, aplicativo de entrega de comida controlado pela investidora holandesa Prosus (PRX.AS) , anunciou nesta terça-feira a compra da Caju, empresa de benefícios corporativos e atuante no mercado de vales-refeição e vales-alimentação. Com a compra da Caju o iFood busca crescer além do seu serviço principal de entregas, mirando também segmento de benefícios a funcionários. O iFood domina o setor de delivery no Brasil, que hoje vive um acirramento da concorrência , após a chegada da Keeta, unidade do gigante chinês de tecnologia Meituan (3690.HK) . Se aprovada pelos órgãos reguladores locais, a aquisição dobrará a presença do iFood no setor de benefícios corporativos, disseram as empresas em um comunicado conjunto. Os termos financeiros do negócio, realizado por meio do iFood Benefícios, braço de benefícios corporativos do iFood, não foram divulgados. No entanto, a aquisição faz parte do plano mais amplo do iFood de investir R$24 bilhões até março de 2027, informou o comunicado. O crescente mercado de vales-refeição e vales-alimentação do Brasil movimenta cerca de R$150 bilhões por ano entre mais de 20 milhões de consumidores, de acordo com Arthur Freitas, CEO do iFood Benefícios. O iFood Benefícios e a Caju processam, cada um, cerca de R$1,3 bilhão em transações mensais, disse Freitas à Reuters em entrevista. Juntas, as duas empresas atenderão aproximadamente 135 mil clientes corporativos e 3 milhões de usuários ativos, acrescentou. O negócio ainda depende da aprovação do Banco Central e do Cade, com conclusão prevista para o próximo ano, segundo Eduardo Del Giglio, cofundador e CEO da Caju.

item.title: Anthropic's public benefit fund and how it compares with other big philanthropic efforts
item.description: Anthropic said it would commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, as debate intensifies over how the growing wealth generated by artificial intelligence should be distributed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic said it would commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, as debate intensifies over how the growing wealth generated by artificial intelligence should be distributed. The pledge comes amid a broader political debate over who should benefit from AI's gains, months after US Senator Bernie Sanders introduced a bill that would give the public a 50% stake in the largest US AI companies. Here is what is known about Anthropic's fund and how it compares with some other large philanthropic efforts set up by major corporations, their current or former leaders, or their families: ANTHROPIC PUBLIC BENEFIT FUND Anthropic [USN:L4N46403A TEXT:"said"] in a blog post on Sunday its Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI's impact on the labor market. The Claude maker said its proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50% increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. OPENAI FOUNDATION OpenAI completed a [USN:L4N3W91HS TEXT:"restructuring"] in October 2025 that left its nonprofit, renamed the OpenAI Foundation, with a 26% stake in the for-profit, worth about $130 billion at the time. The foundation also holds a warrant to receive additional equity if OpenAI Group's share price rises more than tenfold over 15 years. OpenAI said in a blog post at that time that the company's success will raise the value of the nonprofit's stake, which the nonprofit will use to fund its philanthropic work. The foundation said it will initially focus on a $25 billion commitment across two areas: health and curing diseases, and technical solutions to AI resilience. This builds on its $50 million commitment to support nonprofits and mission-focused organizations that OpenAI announced in July 2025. GATES FOUNDATION Founded in 2000 by Microsoft (MSFT.O) co-founder Bill Gates and his then-wife, Melinda French Gates, the Gates Foundation invested more than $102.3 billion during its first 25 years in global health and development, US education and economic mobility. In May 2025, Gates said the foundation would spend an additional $200 billion over the next two decades before winding down in December 2045. The foundation's work through 2045 will focus on three goals: ensuring that no mother or baby dies from a preventable cause, enabling the next generation to grow up without deadly infectious diseases, and helping hundreds of millions of people escape poverty. It plans a record $9 billion payout in 2026, with about 70% of its budget allocated to advancing those first two goals, which encompass its global health work. WARREN BUFFETT'S PLEDGE In 2006, the legendary investor Warren Buffett pledged to donate nearly all of his Berkshire stock to philanthropic foundations. Since then, he has donated over half of his shares, including more than $47 billion to the Gates Foundation and over $17 billion to four family charities. However, he [USN:L6N43G0T3 TEXT:"stopped"] donating to the Gates Foundation following revelations about interactions between Bill Gates and the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, ending a two-decade philanthropic partnership. Buffett said [USN:L2N3MW0D5 TEXT:"that he plans to donate"] 99.5% of his remaining wealth to a charitable trust overseen by his daughter and two sons when he dies. After his death, his children will have about 10 years to give away his remaining wealth and must decide unanimously which philanthropic purposes it should serve. ELON MUSK'S PLEDGE After Anthropic announced its public fund on Sunday, Elon Musk pledged to give one SpaceX share to "every kid in America." "Yes, giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way," the SpaceX and Tesla CEO wrote in an X post. Earlier this year, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband also pledged a share of their SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children under the [USN:L6N43429H TEXT:"Trump Accounts investment initiative"]. MACKENZIE SCOTT'S PLEDGE MacKenzie Scott received about 4% of Amazon's stock in her 2019 divorce from the company's founder Jeff Bezos, a stake then worth about $36 billion. She signed the Giving Pledge shortly after committing to giving away at least half of her Amazon fortune during her lifetime. The Giving Pledge was founded by Buffett and Bill and Melinda Gates to encourage the world's wealthiest people to donate the majority of their fortunes. Since then, she has [USN:L2N2VQ1JR TEXT:"donated"] $275 million to Planned Parenthood (in 2022), more than $4 billion to food banks and emergency relief funds [USN:L3N2NX410 TEXT:"during"] the coronavirus pandemic, and billions of dollars in grants to causes such as racial equality, LGBTQ rights and climate change. Scott gave away $7.1 billion in 2025, according to a Yield Giving letter published last year. FORD FOUNDATION Established by Henry Ford's son Edsel in 1936 with an initial gift of $25,000, the Ford Foundation grew from a family-backed Michigan philanthropy into one of the world's largest foundations. Its current endowment is valued at about $18 billion. The 90-year-old foundation awarded $768 million through 2,288 grants in 2024. Its work is aimed at reducing poverty and injustice, strengthening democratic values and promoting international cooperation. In 2015, it launched BUILD, a five-year, $1 billion investment in the long-term capacity and sustainability of 350 social justice organizations addressing inequality around the world. The foundation renewed BUILD in 2021 with an additional $1 billion. LILLY ENDOWMENT Established in 1937 by J.K. Lilly and his sons through gifts of stock in the family drugmaker, the Lilly Endowment began with a donation of 17,500 shares valued at $262,500. Over its first 88 years, the endowment disbursed nearly $21.3 billion in grants to 11,651 charitable organizations. It paid out $3.85 billion in grants in 2025 while its assets rose to nearly $106 billion. The Indianapolis-based foundation focuses on education, community development and religion, with a particular commitment to Indiana. NOVO NORDISK FOUNDATION Established in Denmark, the Novo Nordisk Foundation traces its origins to August Krogh, H.C. Hagedorn and August Kongsted, who used profits from insulin production to support scientific and humanitarian work. The present foundation took shape in 1989, when the foundations associated with Nordisk and Novo were combined following the merger that created Novo Nordisk. It awarded a record DKK 11.8 billion ($1.77 billion), or about €1.6 billion, across 2,206 grants and philanthropic investments in 2025, up from DKK 10.1 billion in 2024. Its funding primarily supports research and initiatives spanning human health, infectious and cardiometabolic diseases, the green transition and sustainable agriculture. ($1 = 6.6526 Danish crowns)

item.title: Bank of England's Greene says inflation risks are bigger than thought
item.description: Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said the risks of a pickup in broader inflation as a result of the energy price shock from the Iran war were greater than the BoE expected and she reiterated her view that interest rates should go up.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said the risks of a pickup in broader inflation as a result of the energy price shock from the Iran war were greater than the BoE expected and she reiterated her view that interest rates should go up. Greene – part of a minority on the BoE's Monetary Policy Committee that has voted for higher rates – said it was better to act as if the so-called second-round effects from the energy shock were stronger and then adjust policy later if needed. "I therefore continue to believe we should proactively lean against the risk of second-round effects," she said in a speech at the London School of Economics on Tuesday. So far the BoE has not followed the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in increasing borrowing costs in response to the Iran war. But Governor Andrew Bailey, who has backed keeping rates on hold, has [USN:L1N46202H TEXT:"said"] that the longer the conflict goes on, the harder it will be for the BoE not to respond, although he thought inflation pressures remained "quite subdued". Investors expect the BoE will raise its benchmark Bank Rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 4% next month. In her speech, Greene said she believed wage growth was running higher than official data has suggested and pay settlements due in early 2027 might come in higher than thought given inflation was likely to be running around 4% then. She said signs of resilience in Britain's economy this year, despite the energy price jump, added to the case for higher borrowing costs. "It is not obvious to me from this data that our monetary policy stance is meaningfully restrictive," Greene said.

item.title: 英中銀グリーン委員、利上げを主張 「インフレ加速リスク想定以上」
item.description: [ロンドン ２０日 ロイター] - イングランド銀行（ＢＯＥ、英中央銀行）のグリーン金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）委員は２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英中銀グリーン委員、利上げを主張　「インフレ加速リスク想定以上」 3:23 配信

英ロンドンのイングランド銀行（英中央銀行）前で９月撮影。REUTERS/Corey Rudy

[ロンドン ２０日 ロイター] - イングランド銀行（ＢＯＥ、英中央銀行）のグリーン金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）委員は２０日、イラン戦争に伴うエネルギー価格ショックから広範なインフレが加速するリスクは、英中銀の予想を上回っていると述べ、利上げが必要だとの見解を改めて示した。

グリーン氏は、ロンドン・スクール・オブ・エコノミクス（ＬＳＥ）での演説原稿で、エネルギーショックによるいわゆる「二次的波及効果」がより強いと想定して行動し、必要に応じて後から政策を調整する方が望ましいと指摘。

「したがって、私は引き続き『二次的波及効果』のリスクに対して先手を打って対処すべきだと考えている」と述べた。

グリーン氏はＭＰＣの中で、利上げに賛成票を投じてきた少数派の一員。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 10/21(水) 3:23 ロイター

item.title: WWE, McMahons must face sex abuse claims by former 'ring boys'
item.description: A federal judge has denied a bid by World Wrestling Entertainment and former executives Vince and Linda McMahon to dismiss a lawsuit claiming they are liable for years of alleged sexual abuse suffered by teenage "ring boys" in the 1980s and 1990s.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: A federal judge has denied a bid by World Wrestling Entertainment and former executives Vince and Linda McMahon to dismiss a lawsuit claiming they are liable for years of alleged sexual abuse suffered by teenage "ring boys" in the 1980s and 1990s. US District Judge James Bredar in Baltimore on Monday rejected claims that a 2023 Maryland law allowing the plaintiffs to sue over decades-old allegations violated the US Constitution and the defendants' right to due process. The eight anonymous plaintiffs say in the 2024 lawsuit that they were recruited by ringside announcer Melvin Phillips to work as part-time crew members and were abused by him and two other officials at WWE, then known as WWF. Phillips and the other alleged abusers died years before the plaintiffs filed the lawsuit. WWE and lawyers for Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon, the current US Secretary of Education, did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Tuesday. Greg Gutzler, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, said Maryland's law recognizes that "trauma does not follow a legal deadline." “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” Gutzler, of plaintiffs' firm DiCello Levitt, said in a statement. The Maryland law eliminated a seven-year statute of limitations for sex abuse claims involving minors, which had been extended from three years in 2003. It was part of a wave of state laws adopted after the #MeToo movement allowing sex abuse claims previously blocked by statutes of limitations to proceed, in some cases temporarily. The plaintiffs in their lawsuit accused WWE and the McMahons of negligence and negligent hiring and retention, and are seeking unspecified damages. Vince McMahon, who built WWF into a cultural force in the 1980s after purchasing its predecessor from his father, [USN:L1N3EH03B TEXT:"resigned from the organization"] in 2024 amid separate claims of sex trafficking and assault, which [USN:FWN3O60QP TEXT:"he has denied"]. Linda McMahon, his estranged wife, was [USN:L1N3P316M TEXT:"appointed US Secretary of Education"] by President Donald Trump last year after heading the US Small Business Administration during Trump's first term. She and Vince McMahon have previously denied having knowledge of alleged abuse of ring boys. The defendants argued that Maryland's law violated the US Constitution's ban on retroactive, or ex post facto, laws, and that it violated the Constitution's guarantee of due process as applied to them. They said it could be difficult or impossible to mount a defense as witnesses become unavailable, memories fade and other evidence is lost. But Bredar on Monday said the law served a legitimate purpose of addressing the barriers that child sex abuse victims face in court, and that the concerns raised by WWE were overblown. "Plaintiffs can make a case by producing at least some material facts to contest, documents to dispute, and witnesses to cross-examine," the judge wrote. The Maryland Supreme Court last year rejected arguments that the law violated the state's constitution, which Bredar on Monday said had raised distinct issues from the former ring boys' case. But the top courts in several other states including Maine, Utah and Kentucky have said in recent years that similar laws were invalid because expired statutes of limitations are not reversible. The case is Doe v. World Wrestling Entertainment, US District Court for the District of Maryland, No. 1:24-cv-03487. For the plaintiffs: William Murphy of Murphy Falcon & Murphy; Adam Prom and others from DiCello Levitt For WWE: Daniel Toal and others from Paul Weiss Rifkind Wharton & Garrison; Linda Woolf of Goodell DeVries Leech & Dann For Vince McMahon: Christopher Jeffries of Kramon & Graham For Linda McMahon: William Murphy and Samantha Kavanagh of Zuckerman Spaeder Read more: [USN:L1N3EH03B TEXT:"Vince McMahon resigns from TKO, WWE over sex assault lawsuit"] [USN:L1N3P316M TEXT:"Trump's pick for education chief, Linda McMahon, defends plans to unwind the department"] [USN:FWN3O60QP TEXT:"Former WWE CEO Vince McMahon settles with SEC over undisclosed settlements with women"]

Oct 20 : SpaceX shareholders want to know when the rocket maker will merge with Tesla, bringing together two of Elon Musk's biggest companies in a union that investors have long speculated about. "When will SpaceX merge with Tesla?" was the second-most upvoted question — drawing 26 upvotes — submitted by investors to SpaceX management ahead of its third-quarter earnings webcast on Tuesday. The same question received 128 upvotes on the Tesla investor relations site.  Barclays suggested last week that a deal could be announced before Tesla's annual meeting, with SpaceX the likelier acquirer, though neither company nor Musk has officially committed to favoring a deal. The top-voted question, with 38 upvotes, was on the progress of Starship's lunar lander hardware, in a list that showed retail investors were focused on Starship while analysts and institutional shareholders pressed for detail on AI revenue and spending.  SpaceX has made progress testing Starship, but key technologies needed to turn the giant rocket into a lunar lander, including refueling it in orbit, have yet to be fully demonstrated. The company's profitable satellite internet service, Starlink, is helping bankroll heavy spending on chips, terrestrial data centers and Grok, but losses at the AI businesses have ballooned. While the investor questions list ahead of its second-quarter earnings in August was topped by lighthearted, meme-driven submissions, this quarter's top questions leaned more toward corporate plans, with novelty entries mostly near the bottom. It was not clear which questions executives would take when the webcast starts at 4:30 p.m. EDT (2030 GMT). "What share of AI revenue is now under multi-year commitments, and what gives management confidence AI can grow at or above the company's overall rate for several years?" a prospective investor asked, earning no upvotes. SpaceX's AI revenue comes from a handful of customers, including Alphabet's Google and AI lab Anthropic, and the compute contracts can be terminated on about 90 days' notice. One institutional investor asked how much contracted Google capacity would stay available if a court halted gas turbines at the Colossus 2 data center in Memphis, Tennessee. Another asked whether Google had accepted the full capacity under its cloud agreement and whether SpaceX expected to earn the full contractual monthly rate. An analyst's six-part question on Starlink satellite capacity, launch priorities and capital spending drew no upvotes. Lighter submissions were scattered through the list. One user asked whether SpaceX would land a Tesla Roadster — a sports car with rocket thrusters for short jumps in the air — on the moon, adding, "(it) would be awesome."

Source: Reuters
